text: Persina Nature Park (Bulgarian: Природен парк Персина) is a wetland area on the Bulgarian side of the Danube, established on December 4, 2000. It spans 21,762 ha (53,780 acres) and lies within the territories of three municipalities: Nikopol, Belene, and Svishtov. The park's primary goal is the conservation and restoration of Danube wetlands, with special focus on the numerous islands and their natural condition. Named after Persin Island, which is part of the Belene Islands Complex, the island is 15 km (9.3 mi) long and 6 km (3.7 mi) wide, making it the fourth largest Danube island and the largest in Bulgaria. A separate island group near Nikopol is also significant and was designated a Ramsar site on September 24, 2002, covering 18,330 ha (45,300 acres), the largest such site in Bulgaria. Key ecosystems within the park include flooded forests along the Danube and inland marshes, and several protected areas have been created to safeguard these habitats.
